questions: Can the edge-reversal operation be performed multiple times, and does each reversal toggle the direction of all edges (i.e., after an odd number of reversals, edges are reversed; after an even number, they are back to original)?
Is the edge-reversal operation instantaneous and global, affecting all edges simultaneously, or does it only affect edges from the current vertex?
After reversing edges, can you move along a newly created directed edge in the same step, or must you wait until the next operation?
Are self-loops (u_i = v_i) allowed, and if so, how do they behave under reversal?
Is the cost X incurred every time you reverse edges, regardless of whether the graph state changes (e.g., reversing twice in a row)?
Can you reverse edges even if no outgoing edge exists from your current vertex, or is reversal always allowed?
Is the goal to reach vertex N exactly, or is it acceptable to pass through N and continue moving?
Do we consider the graph as static between reversals, meaning edges don't change direction except when explicitly reversed?
